transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Hi Leo, I'm going to ask you and your mum some questions today. There are no right or wrong answers. Is that okay?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mum, can you tell me what prompted the referral?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: His teacher, Ms Patel, sent a note home in October saying he's struggling to finish written work and he's often out of his seat. We'd noticed homework was a battle too.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, what's school like for you?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: It's okay. I like maths and PE. I don't like writing because it takes forever.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What happens when you have to write something?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: I start and then I think about other stuff. Like Minecraft. And then the time is over.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you get out of your seat in class?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Sometimes. To sharpen my pencil. Ms Patel says I do it too much.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mum, how many times has the school contacted you this term?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Twice. The October note, and a phone call last week.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Was the phone call about the same things?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Partly. It was mainly that he'd pushed another boy in the lunch queue. According to Leo, the other boy had pushed in front of him first.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, can you tell me about that?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Jayden pushed in front of me so I pushed him back. I said sorry after.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mum, has anything like that happened before?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Not at school, no. He and his sister squabble at home, but that's normal sibling stuff, I think.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How does homework go at home?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: It takes an hour for something that should take twenty minutes. I have to sit next to him or he drifts off.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is that every night?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Every night we have homework, so four nights a week.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, do you have friends at school?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Yeah, lots. Me and Omar and Sami play football every break.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mum, what's your sense of his friendships?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Honestly, I worry. He doesn't get invited to birthday parties much. I think he only really has Omar.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, do you get invited to parties?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Sometimes. I went to Sami's party.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do the other kids ever leave you out?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: No. Well, once in the playground they said I couldn't play tag because I always change the rules.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How did that feel?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Annoying. But then we played football instead.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mum, does he find it hard to take turns or to wait?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Yes, with board games especially. He'll grab the dice. He's better with his grandad, funnily enough. Grandad is very patient with him.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Let's talk about routines at home. What time does Leo go to bed?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Lights out at half past eight, but he's often still awake at ten.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, what do you do when you can't sleep?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: I read with my torch. Or I just think about stuff.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Does he use screens before bed?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: He has the tablet until about eight. We stopped it at bedtime about a month ago, and I'm not sure it's made a difference yet.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is he tired in the mornings?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Very hard to wake. Some mornings it's a real fight to get him to school on time.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has he always been a poor sleeper?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Since he was a toddler, really.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How has his mood been?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: Mostly happy. He gets frustrated with homework and sometimes says he's stupid.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, do you ever feel like that?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: When I can't do the writing. Not other times.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is there anything you worry about a lot?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Spiders. And whether I'll get picked for the football team.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mum, were there any concerns about his development when he was younger, like speech or walking?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: No, everything was on time. He was an early talker, actually.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is there any family history of attention or learning difficulties?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: My brother was diagnosed with dyslexia at school. Nothing else that I know of.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has Leo had his eyes and hearing checked?

transcript.speaker: parent1
transcript.text: His hearing was checked last year and it was fine. Eyes, not recently.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Leo, if you could change one thing about school, what would it be?

transcript.speaker: child1
transcript.text: Less writing. And a longer break.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Thank you both. That's really helpful.

assessment.label: School and attention
assessment.text: Teacher has reported difficulty completing written work and frequent out-of-seat behaviour, first raised in October. Leo describes losing focus during writing tasks as his thoughts drift to other topics. Leo acknowledges that he leaves his seat too often. Has had repeated physical altercations with peers at school. Homework takes about an hour on four nights a week and needs a parent sitting alongside him.

assessment.label: Peer relationships
assessment.text: Leo reports that he is rarely invited to birthday parties and has only one close friend. Was once excluded from a playground game by peers for changing the rules. Has difficulty waiting his turn in games, consistently across all the adults who play with him.

assessment.label: Sleep and home routines
assessment.text: Long-standing difficulty settling at night since toddlerhood, often still awake at ten despite lights out at half past eight. Removing the tablet at bedtime has not improved his sleep. Frequently describes himself as stupid. Developmental milestones were on time; hearing was normal last year, and vision has not been checked recently. Presentation raises the possibility of ADHD, combined presentation.
